status: post-hoc conditional permutation diagnostic; not a causal test

protocol.permutation_unit: for each outer fold, shuffle only training trace labels within each benchmark/task group; each group is wholly assigned to train or test; held-out labels remain untouched
protocol.association_training_pairs: fixed to the original mode-stratified pairs to isolate the mode-score feature; not resampled or relabeled
protocol.gallery: same two protocols as the specificity controls; Human-to-Agent queries only
protocol.statistic: primary: Human-to-Agent benchmark-macro Recall@1 paired delta (permuted mode-aware ranker minus similarity-only); compare this delta with the observed real-label delta
protocol.primary_protocol: full_gallery; heldout_gallery is a secondary robustness protocol
protocol.target_mapping: one shuffled mapping per outer-fold training set is reused for inner OOF and final mode-head fitting; no held-out mode label enters model fitting
protocol.rng: numpy.default_rng (PCG64); one seeded stream across permutations and folds

interpretation_limits: The result tests trace-specific mode-label alignment conditional on task composition; it does not estimate a causal effect of Agent execution.
Mode labels remain confounded with collection pathway, so a small permutation p-value cannot distinguish execution behavior from logger or interface artifacts.
The reported upper-tail fraction is an exploratory training-label negative control, not a population-level p-value; it depends on within-task exchangeability.
This 999-permutation run has empirical-tail resolution 1/1000; all 40 task groups have already been explored, so the result remains post-hoc rather than independent confirmation.
Permutation reference intervals describe the shuffled-label distribution, not confidence intervals for a population effect.
